feed.text: U19 Asia Cup: India U19 lose to Pakistan U19 by 3 wickets — Arjun Rajput's 107 helps India to 208, but Hamza Zahoor's unbeaten 100 wins it for Pakistan with 11 balls left.
AWCL: East Bengal lose 0–2 to April 25 SC in Kolkata but go through to the quarter-finals — the first Indian club to reach that stage.
2nd ODI, Wellington: India beat New Zealand by 4 runs (DLS) after rain ended play — NZ 134 in 41 overs, India 113/7 in 26. Gurnoor Brar is Player of the Match; India lead 2–0.
ISL: East Bengal lose 3–5 at Chennaiyin FC — Brison Fernandes scores twice in the first 18 minutes; Chennaiyin's first win of the season.
ISL: Inter Kashi lose 0–3 to SC Delhi in Pune — Fortes, Peña and Rodriguinho score.
Chennai Open: Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi's dream run ends in the quarter-final, 3-6 3-6 to Robin Montgomery.
ISL: FC Goa lose 1–2 at home to Bengaluru FC — Soham Varshneya's 90+3' winner after Borja Martínez and Franchu scored.
U19 Asia Cup: India U19 beat Nepal by 10 wickets — Ishan Sood 3/18, then Aaryavir Sehwag 70* and Lakshya Raichandani 53* chase 129 in 19.1 overs. Pakistan next on Sunday.

Silver for Tanvi Patri at the Youth Olympics: the 15-year-old loses a thriller 21–15, 13–21, 24–26 to China's Zhang Yixin after saving six match points — India's first women's badminton medal at the Games.
India are Asian Champions Trophy winners again: a 4–1 comeback win over Japan in Mohali (Lakra, Dilpreet, Jugraj, Vivek Sagar after Japan led 1–0) for a record sixth title.
SAFF Championship: India beat Pakistan 3–2 in Dhaka — Suhail Bhat 2, Kipgen 1 — as Pakistan scored twice in stoppage time.
ISL: Mohun Bagan beat Odisha 3–2 with Lee Erwin's 88th-minute winner to go top; NorthEast United beat Churchill Brothers 2–0.
Chennai Open: Indian No. 1 Vaishnavi Adkar goes out in the Round of 16 to 7th seed Zakharova; Maaya Rajeshwaran is India's last singles hope.
Ranji Trophy Round 4 ends: Maharashtra beat Bengal by 10 wickets, Tamil Nadu (Paul 208) and Karnataka win by an innings, Mumbai beat Railways by 106 runs.
History in Chennai: 17-year-old Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi beats Falkowska 6-4 6-3 — first Indian woman in a WTA singles quarter-final since Sania Mirza in 2012. Next: Robin Montgomery (USA) on 6 Nov.
